t: Rescans and Scan Limits in AI & Search Visibility
html:
Rescanning your website helps you check whether SEO fixes have improved its technical health. AI & Search Visibility lets you run additional audits after making changes, with a limit of 10 audits per project per monthly cycle during the beta. Knowing when to rescan helps you use your available audits effectively.

What Are SEO Audit Rescans?


A rescan runs a new SEO audit of your website to identify current issues and generate updated results. Comparing the new health score and findings with your previous report helps you evaluate the changes you've made.


Rescanning after making SEO improvements helps you verify results without unnecessarily using your monthly audit allowance.


  • Verify SEO Fixes: Check whether previously identified issues are still detected.

  • Measure Improvements: Review your updated health score, errors, warnings, and notices.

  • Identify Remaining Issues: Find problems that still need attention after your changes.

When Should You Rescan Your Website?


Run a rescan after addressing the issues identified in your previous audit. Repeatedly scanning without making changes may use your available audits without providing useful new information.


For example, a test website initially received a health score of 73/100. After fixing several issues and rescanning, its score increased to 93/100.


This is an example from one website; results will vary depending on the issues identified and the changes made.


Tip: Review your action items, complete the relevant fixes, and then rescan to evaluate the results.

How to Run an SEO Audit Rescan


Rescanning generates updated audit findings based on your website's current condition.


  1. Open AI & Search Visibility and select your project.

  2. Navigate to SEO Audit.

  3. Open the existing audit report and select the available Rescan option.

  4. Allow the scan to complete.

  5. Review the updated health score and detected issues to evaluate your improvements.


Understanding SEO Audit Beta Limits


Each project has a fixed audit allowance during the beta. The limit applies to standard and advanced audits combined.


Beta LimitAllowance
Audits per Project10 per monthly cycle
Audit TypesStandard and advanced combined
When the Limit Is ReachedAdditional audits become unavailable, but the latest completed report remains accessible.

What Happens When You Reach the Audit Limit?


Once you've used the 10 available audits for a project, you cannot run another audit until additional scans become available in a subsequent monthly cycle.


The last completed audit report remains available, along with a prompt encouraging you to work on its recommended fixes.


You can continue reviewing existing findings and addressing issues without running another scan.
